summary: Merrimack County, NH summit in Allenstown; the FFLA list marks its tower gone, and a March 2020 hiker found only the former tower's foundations below the summit.

facts.status_note: Only the foundations of the former tower remain, just below the summit, per a March 2020 hiking report

access.note: Reached on foot from the park gate lot on Podunk Road; the park gates were closed on the March 2020 visit

visit.trail_note: Bear Hill Trail runs 1.2 miles to the summit from where it meets Podunk Road, per the 2020 hiking report

evidence.supports: FFLA lists a tower at Bear Hill, Merrimack County, and marks it gone
foundations of the former tower just below the summit, and anthills
evidence.quote: Just below the summit are the foundations of the former fire tower and lots of anthills

evidence.supports: walked down Podunk Road to the Bear Hill Trail
evidence.quote: We walked down Podunk Road until we reached Bear Hill Trail

evidence.supports: parking at the gate lot on Podunk Road
evidence.quote: we parked in the hiker/biker lot at the gates on Podunk Road
the gates to the park are still closed

evidence.supports: 1.2 miles from the Bear Hill Trail junction to the summit
evidence.quote: From here it is 1.2 miles to the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The blog's NH list does not tag Bear Hill as no longer standing, but its March 2020 trip report describes only the foundations of the former tower, which matches the FFLA entry Tower Gone.

notes_for_editor: Built date, builder, design, height and staffing are not in any source read; the record's design and height stay empty. The Forest Lookouts Bear Hill page has only a county line. The trip report calls the park 'Bear Book State Park' (apparently a typo for Bear Brook), so the story does not name the park. The only site description is one 2020 visit, so the status rests on that plus the FFLA entry. The park is treated as public because the hike used its trail and parking; this is medium confidence. Facts agency is omitted because no source names one. Record fields are otherwise consistent (coordinates match FFLA).
